title: Théorie de Kumer ? + note Alexandre (bi tenseur…) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the previous page's theme. There, involutive bitorsors (X∘X ≅ 1) were identified with involutions of π up to inner automorphisms, i.e. with extensions 1→π→π̃→Z/2→1. Here the theme is made concrete in two ways.

(1) A real structure on a punctured sphere. Take π = π_1 of P^1 minus four real points (the sketch shows 0, 1, -1 and ∞ on the real equator; i and -i are the poles). The generators λ_0,…,λ_3 are loops around the punctures. Under the path-composition convention the relation is λ_3λ_2λ_1λ_0 = 1; λ_0λ_1λ_2λ_3 = 1 is crossed out.
- ε is complex conjugation, an antiholomorphic involution with ε^2 = 1.
- The chosen base point i is not real; conjugation sends it to ī = -i.
- Grothendieck therefore works in the fundamental groupoid on the base points {i, -i}: Hom(i,i) ≃ π, Hom(-i,-i) ≃ π, and Hom(i,-i) is a bitorsor between them.
- Conjugation of a loop λ at i is the composite i →(ε^{-1}) ī →(λ̄) ī →(ε) i, written ε∘λ̄_i∘ε^{-1}. This is exactly the bitorsor-squared-trivial situation of the previous page, made explicit for a real variety.
- For loops around real punctures, with suitable paths, the relations are ελ_0ε^{-1} = λ_0^{-1}, ελ_1ε^{-1} = λ_1^{-1}, and ελ_2ε^{-1} = λ_1^{-1}λ_2^{-1}λ_1 (a conjugate of an inverse).
- This gives the semidirect product π ⋊ Z/2 = π_1 of the real variety (Gal(C/R)-extended fundamental group). It is the topological counterpart of the 'cartes' and (Z/2)^{*I} on the previous page: reflection groups and non-oriented maps versus oriented ones.

(2) A general construction: the fundamental group of a space X with a group Γ acting, π_1(X,Γ,a).
- Elements are pairs (γ ∈ Γ, l ∈ Hom(γa, a)), with l a homotopy class of paths.
- The product is (γ',l')(γ,l) = (γ'γ, l'∘γ'(l)), obtained from the chain γ'γa →(γ'(l)) γ'b →(l') c.
- There is a homomorphism π_1(X,Γ,a) → Γ with kernel π_1(X,a); it is surjective when X is connected.
- In modern terms this is the fundamental group of the quotient stack/orbifold [X/Γ], i.e. the equivariant fundamental group. Applied to Γ = Z/2 acting by conjugation it recovers (1).

The next page goes on to bitorsors, composition of the functors Ens(π)→Ens(π'), and the classification π_0(Bit(π',π)) ≅ Isomext(π',π).
errors: An intermediate attempt uses the opposite convention, l: a → γb, giving (γγ', (γl')∘l) with target γγ'c. This conflicts with the convention l: γa → b used elsewhere on the page. Grothendieck crosses it out and corrects it to (γ'γ, l'∘γ'(l)), which is consistent and associative.
The relation λ_0λ_1λ_2λ_3 = 1 is crossed out and replaced by λ_3λ_2λ_1λ_0 = 1. This is a convention fix for composition of paths, not a mathematical error.
Exactly which paths make ελ_iε^{-1} = λ_i^{-1} hold for i = 0, 1 is only implicit in the sketches. As stated, the relations depend on choosing paths compatible with the conjugation.

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid with two conjugate base points i, -i, and the action of complex conjugation expressed as an involutive bitorsor / extension of Z/2 by π
ideas.modern_name: Real structure on π_1; π_1(X(C)) ⋊ Gal(C/R); Galois action on fundamental groupoids with several base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Galois action on π_1 in SGA1); real case studied by many, e.g. Cox, Huisman; used in the theory of real dessins and multi-based groupoids
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (Galois action on π_1); Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche (groupoids with several base points, Galois action on P^1 minus points)

ideas.what: Explicit action of conjugation on standard generators of π_1(P^1 minus 4 real points): λ ↦ λ^{-1} up to conjugation
ideas.modern_name: Complex conjugation on the Artin/standard generators of the 4-punctured sphere (M_{0,4} level)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (Ihara and others for Galois actions on π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}))

ideas.modern_name: Equivariant / orbifold fundamental group; π_1 of the quotient stack [X/Γ]

deep.surprise_reason: Standard material: the equivariant fundamental group and conjugation acting on π_1 of a punctured sphere via conjugate base points. It is worked out as an illustration of the involutive-bitorsor / Ext(Z/2,π) dictionary from the previous page. Nothing appears new relative to the literature or to Grothendieck's own Longue Marche and Esquisse themes.
transcription_corrections: The symbols transcribed as '𝔲_π' under Hom(-i,-i) and Hom(i,i) are most likely '≃ π' (or '≈ π'), indicating that each vertex group is isomorphic to π.
The relation λ_1^{-1}λ_2^{-1}λ_1 written near the sketches is presumably the value of ελ_2ε^{-1}.
In the middle derivation, '[-...-] γγ' c' and 'a →((γl')∘l) γγ'c' belong to a discarded convention (l: a→γb). The final boxed law is (γ',l')(γ,l) = (γ'γ, l'∘γ'(l)).
The sphere sketch labels points i (top), -i (bottom), 1 and -1 (equator ends), and 0 (centre), so π is π_1 of the sphere minus four real points.
